payload.text:
Radial-velocity dataset seed1743_diff2.

- 80 observations over a baseline of 30.1 days
- median reported uncertainty: 0.965 m/s
- instruments: instA
- host star mass: 0.949 solar masses
- submission attempts available: 3

Recover the planetary system that produced this signal: the number of
planets and each one's orbital parameters. The data is available to your
tools; you do not need it inlined here.

A submission passes only if it satisfies all four criteria at once: the
model must beat a flat line (delta-BIC), the residual scatter must be
within 1.5x the median reported uncertainty, the orbits must match the
underlying system, and the planet count must be right. A good statistical
fit at the wrong period fails.

Strongly supported simplest hypothesis: 1 planet at 11.16 days.

Why:
- The 11.163 d peak is overwhelmingly dominant (power 0.832, FAP ~ 0), far above all others.
- It is not coincident with the main spectral-window periods (~0.503, 0.610, 0.737 d), so it is unlikely to be cadence-induced.
- Nearby notable peaks are consistent with aliases/harmonics rather than distinct planets:
  - 5.80 d is very close to the half-period/harmonic of 11.16 d (11.16/2 = 5.58 d; also 2×5.80 = 11.59 d), so I would not promote it as a separate planet.
  - 1.08 d is close to the 1-day beat alias of 11.16 d (listed beat_1d_minus = 1.098 d).
  - 0.50–0.70 d peaks overlap the spectral window structure and have weak significance.

So the engineer should first fit a 1-planet Keplerian with period initialized near 11.16 d, then inspect residuals for any surviving coherent signal before adding complexity.

HANDOFF: engineer
